header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

The DeepSeek Harness implementation checkout is at __FDE_APP_PATH__/. The checkout location and current working directory are separate values and may differ; never infer the working directory from this path. Use pwd to determine the current working directory. Use this checkout only to inspect or extend DSH itself.

You are interacting with the user through the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI at http://127.0.0.1:3080. When the user refers to "this page", "this GUI", or "this app" without naming another target, they mean this GUI. The browser provides no implicit DOM, route, or screenshot context. The client-plugin HMR receiver is active, but client-plugin changes reload without a refresh only while `pnpm run dev:web` is also running from this same checkout to rebuild their bundles; verify that watcher before promising automatic updates. Every other change — the apps/web shell and plain packages — requires rebuilding the affected Web artifacts and verifying this existing URL after a page refresh. Starting another server does not update this GUI. The apps/web Vite entry builds the shell but is not a standalone application because only dsh web injects window.__DSH_BOOT__. Do not start a replacement server unless the user asks; if one is needed, use a managed background job and verify its exact URL.

You are a coding agent powered by the deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp model. Your working directory is __FDE_WORKSPACE_PATH__.

Paths prefixed with @ are files explicitly referenced by the user. Use the read tool when their contents are needed; do not claim to have inspected a file before reading it.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use the web_search tool to discover current information on the web. The required queries array accepts 1–4 non-empty search queries; use a one-item array for a single search. It returns an optional answer plus a list of source URLs. Use the returned source snippets when available, and cite the relevant URLs as markdown links.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Use subagent_fork in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

When you successfully create or modify files, mention the primary outputs in your final response. To make those and any other changed-file references clickable in Web, format them as Markdown inline code using the exact file-tool path, or a basename when unique among the files changed in that turn.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

<content>
1: # DS4-AI数据分析系统学员版
2: 
3: DS4-AI数据分析系统是一套本地优先的单用户数据分析工作台。系统把数据源接入、只读查询、数据探索、特征工程、机器学习、产物血缘、报告编排和可扩展 Skills 组织在同一个项目工作区中。
4: 
5: ## 一、领取并解压项目包
6: 
7: 向助教领取 `DS4-AI数据分析系统-学员版.zip`。项目源码包不包含真实 API Key、个人数据库连接、运行数据库和原始 Olist 数据。
8: 
9: macOS、Linux 或 WSL2 可在保存压缩包的目录执行：
10: 
11: ```bash
12: unzip 'DS4-AI数据分析系统-学员版.zip'
13: cd 'DS4-AI数据分析系统'
14: ```
15: 
16: Windows PowerShell 可先完成解压，再从 WSL2 进入解压目录：
17: 
18: ```powershell
19: Expand-Archive -Path '.\DS4-AI数据分析系统-学员版.zip' -DestinationPath '.'
20: ```
21: 
22: 项目启动与沙箱脚本使用 Bash、POSIX 进程信号和 Unix 文件权限。Windows 学员应使用 WSL2；当前学员版没有把 PowerShell 原生运行列为已验证路径。
23: 
24: ## 二、环境要求
25: 
26: 基础运行需要：
27: 
28: - Python 3.12；
29: - uv；
30: - Node.js 22 或更高版本；
31: - pnpm；
32: - 8 GB 以上内存，推荐 16 GB；
33: - 浏览器使用 Chromium、Chrome 或 Edge 的当前稳定版本。
34: 
35: Docker Desktop 只在执行脚本型 Skill 时需要。MySQL 只在连接 MySQL 数据源或复现实验数据时需要；CSV、Excel 和 SQLite 主路径不依赖 MySQL。
36: 
37: 检查本机版本：
38: 
39: ```bash
40: python3.12 --version
41: uv --version
42: node --version
43: pnpm --version
44: ```
45: 
46: ## 三、安装依赖
47: 
48: 以下命令均在解压后的 `DS4-AI数据分析系统` 根目录执行：
49: 
50: ```bash
51: uv sync --group dev
52: pnpm --dir frontend install --frozen-lockfile
53: pnpm --dir frontend exec playwright install chromium
54: ```
55: 
56: 第一条命令在 `.venv/` 中安装后端与开发测试依赖；第二条命令严格按照前端锁文件安装依赖；第三条命令安装浏览器端到端测试所需的 Chromium。
57: 
58: ## 四、准备本地配置
59: 
60: 复制公开配置示例：
61: 
62: ```bash
63: cp .env.example .env
64: chmod 600 .env
65: ```
66: 
67: 模型凭证不写入源码包或 `.env.example`。系统无需在线模型即可运行项目管理、数据接入、查询、图表、机器学习、报告版本和产物管理等确定性能力。需要在线对话时，启动系统后进入“设置 → 模型服务”，填写 API Key、模型名称和 Base URL，并先执行连接测试再保存；凭证将以权限为 `600` 的运行时文件保存在本机 `.runtime/` 中。
68: 
69: ## 五、启动、状态检查与停止
70: 
71: 依赖安装完成后使用项目脚本启动前后端：
72: 
73: ```bash
74: ./scripts/start.sh
75: ```
76: 
77: 启动脚本只负责启动已经安装好的后端和前端，不会代替依赖安装。浏览器访问 `http://127.0.0.1:5173`，后端健康接口为 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health`。
78: 
79: 检查服务状态：
80: 
81: ```bash
82: curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health
83: curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:5173/
84: ```
85: 
86: 停止本项目启动的前后端进程：
87: 
88: ```bash
89: ./scripts/stop.sh
90: ```
91: 
92: 停止脚本不会删除 `.runtime/` 中的项目、数据源、模型、报告与设置。需要彻底重置时，应先备份所需项目，再手动删除 `.runtime/`。
93: 
94: 若默认端口已被占用，可在启动时指定另一组端口：
95: 
96: ```bash
97: NORTHLIGHT_API_PORT=18100 NORTHLIGHT_WEB_PORT=15180 ./scripts/start.sh
98: ```
99: 
100: 此时浏览器地址为 `http://127.0.0.1:15180`，API 健康接口为 `http://127.0.0.1:18100/api/health`。停止命令仍为 `./scripts/stop.sh`。
101: 
102: ## 六、第一个分析项目
103: 
104: 1. 在首页创建一个分析项目。
105: 2. 在“数据资产”或项目数据源页面上传 CSV、Excel 或 SQLite 文件。
106: 3. 返回项目对话页并选择本轮数据源。
107: 4. 使用自然语言提出查询、图表、数据质量、特征工程或建模任务。
108: 5. 在右侧“运行、结果、报告”区域检查执行步骤、产物与报告版本。
109: 6. 在产物页查看数据、SQL、代码、图表、模型、预测和报告之间的血缘关系。
110: 
111: Olist 演示数据不随源码包重复分发。需要复现课程中的巴西电商分析时，可向助教领取对应数据文件，或从数据集发布页自行下载后放入 `.runtime/datasets/olist/olist.zip`，再执行：
112: 
113: ```bash
114: uv run python scripts/prepare_olist.py
115: ```
116: 
117: ## 七、可选能力
118: 
119: 执行脚本型 Skill 前，启动 Docker Desktop 并构建无网络沙箱镜像：
120: 
121: ```bash
122: ./scripts/build-sandbox.sh
123: ```
124: 
125: macOS Apple Silicon 上的本地 MySQL 8.4 演示环境可由项目脚本手动管理：
126: 
127: ```bash
128: ./scripts/mysql-local.sh start
129: ./scripts/mysql-local.sh status
130: ./scripts/mysql-local.sh stop
131: ```
132: 
133: Linux 或 WSL2 可连接已有 MySQL 8.x 实例；项目自带的 `mysql-local.sh` 使用 Homebrew 安装路径，不属于 Linux 与 Windows 原生启动脚本。
134: 
135: ## 八、构建与测试
136: 
137: 后端静态检查、类型检查与测试：
138: 
139: ```bash
140: uv run ruff check backend scripts
141: uv run mypy backend/northlight
142: uv run pytest -q
143: ```
144: 
145: 前端单元测试、生产构建与浏览器端到端测试：
146: 
147: ```bash
148: pnpm --dir frontend test
149: pnpm --dir frontend build
150: NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost pnpm --dir frontend test:e2e
151: ```
152: 
153: 百万行数据性能诊断属于可选步骤：
154: 
155: ```bash
156: uv run python scripts/benchmark_million.py
157: ```
158: 
159: ## 九、常见问题
160: 
161: - API 未就绪：检查 `.runtime/logs/api.log`，确认 8000 端口未被其他进程占用。
162: - 页面无法访问 API：确认 5173 端口未被占用，并为 localhost 设置 `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`。
163: - 在线聊天提示没有凭证：进入设置页完成模型连接测试；这不影响本地确定性能力。
164: - 报告没有图表：报告只嵌入明确引用的图表产物，应先保存图表，再创建新报告版本。
165: - 数据源显示已变化：重新执行画像后再查询，避免沿用过期字段基线。
166: - Skill 脚本无法运行：确认 Docker Desktop 已启动，并已构建 `northlight-python-sandbox:0.1` 镜像。

(End of file - total 166 lines)
</content>

13: record_matches() {
14:   local pid_file="$1"
15:   local expected="$2"
16:   [[ -f "${pid_file}" ]] || return 1
17:   local pid signature current
18:   IFS=$'\t' read -r pid signature <"${pid_file}" || return 1
19:   [[ "${signature}" == "${expected}" ]] || return 1
20:   current="$(ps -p "${pid}" -o command= 2>/dev/null || true)"
21:   [[ -n "${current}" && "${current}" == *"${expected}"* ]]
22: }
23: 
24: stop_owned_process() {
25:   local name="$1"
26:   local signature="$2"
27:   local pid_file="${runtime_root}/${name}.pid"
28:   if record_matches "${pid_file}" "${signature}"; then
29:     local pid

32:   fi

41:   last_start=0

45:   fi

47:   (
48:     cd "${project_root}"
49:     nohup "$@" >"${log_root}/${name}.log" 2>&1 &
50:     printf '%s\t%s\n' "$!" "${signature}" >"${pid_file}"
51:   )
52:   last_start=1
53: }

58:     touch "${runtime_root}/mysql-owned-by-app"
59:   fi
60: fi

75:   fi

{"file_path": "__FDE_WORKSPACE_PATH__/INSTALL.md", "content": "# 安装说明

本文档说明如何在本机安装并运行该项目。

本项目是一套**本地优先的单用户数据分析工作台**，把数据源接入、只读查询、数据探索、特征工程、机器学习、产物血缘、报告编排和可扩展 Skills 组织在同一个项目工作区中。它不需要云端服务即可运行项目管理、数据接入、查询、图表、机器学习、报告版本和产物管理等确定性能力；仅“在线对话/模型服务”需要填写模型 API Key。

> 本文档默认以已解压的项目源码根目录为当前工作目录。文中所有命令均在根目录执行。

---

## 一、环境要求

运行本项目需要：

- **Python 3.12**（`requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`）；
- **uv**（Python 依赖管理工具）；
- **Node.js 22 或更高版本**；
- **pnpm**（前端包管理器）；
- 内存 **8 GB 以上，推荐 16 GB**；
- 浏览器使用 **Chromium、Chrome 或 Edge** 的当前稳定版本。

**可选**：

- **Docker Desktop**：仅在执行脚本型 Skill 时需要；
- **MySQL**：仅在连接 MySQL 数据源或复现实验数据时需要。CSV、Excel 和 SQLite 主路径不依赖 MySQL。

先检查本机版本：

```bash
python3.12 --version
uv --version
node --version
pnpm --version
```

> Windows 用户：项目启动与沙箱脚本使用 Bash、POSIX 进程信号和 Unix 文件权限。建议使用 **WSL2** 运行；当前版本未把 PowerShell 原生运行列为已验证路径。

---

## 二、安装依赖

以下命令均在项目根目录执行。

### 1. 安装后端依赖（含开发/测试依赖）

```bash
uv sync --group dev
```

该命令会在项目根目录创建 `.venv/` 虚拟环境，并按 `pyproject.toml` 与 `uv.lock` 安装后端依赖（DuckDB、FastAPI、pandas、polars、scikit-learn、SQLAlchemy 等）以及 `dev` 组的开发测试依赖（mypy、pytest、ruff 等）。

### 2. 安装前端依赖

```bash
pnpm --dir frontend install --frozen-lockfile
```

严格按照 `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml` 锁文件安装 `frontend/` 下的依赖。

### 3. 安装浏览器测试运行时

```bash
pnpm --dir frontend exec playwright install chromium
```

安装浏览器端到端测试所需要的 Chromium（仅在执行端到端测试时需要，可跳过）。

---

## 三、准备本地配置

复制公开配置示例并收紧文件权限：

```bash
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
```

`.env` 默认内容（见 `.env.example`）：

```ini
NORTHLIGHT_RUNTIME_ROOT=.runtime
NORTHLIGHT_MODEL_NAME=deepseek-v4-flash
NORTHLIGHT_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com
```

> 模型凭证不会写入源码包或 `.env`。需要在线对话时，启动后进入“设置 → 模型服务”，填写 API Key、模型名称和 Base URL，先执行连接测试再保存；凭证将作为权限为 `600` 的运行时文件保存在 `.runtime/` 中。这不影响本地确定性能力。

---

## 四、启动、状态检查与停止

### 启动

依赖安装完成后，使用项目脚本一次性启动后端与前端：

```bash
./scripts/start.sh
```

启动脚本只负责启动**已安装好**的后端和前端，不会代替依赖安装。

- 浏览器地址：`http://127.0.0.1:5173`
- 后端健康接口：`http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health`

### 状态检查

```bash
curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health
curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:5173/
```

### 停止

```bash
./scripts/stop.sh
```

停止脚本不会删除 `.runtime/` 中的项目、数据源、模型、报告与设置。需要彻底重置时，先备份所需项目，再手动删除 `.runtime/`。

### 指定其他端口

若默认端口被占用，可指定另外一组端口启动：

```bash
NORTHLIGHT_API_PORT=18100 NORTHLIGHT_WEB_PORT=15180 ./scripts/start.sh
```

此时浏览器地址为 `http://127.0.0.1:15180`，API 健康接口为 `http://127.0.0.1:18100/api/health`。停止命令仍为 `./scripts/stop.sh`。

---

## 五、可选能力

---

- **Python 3.12**（`requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`）；

- **Node.js 22 或更高版本**；
- **pnpm**（前端包管理器）；
- 内存 **8 GB 以上，推荐 16 GB**；
- 浏览器使用 **Chromium、Chrome 或 Edge** 的当前稳定版本。

**可选**：

- **Docker Desktop**：仅在执行脚本型 Skill 时需要；
- **MySQL**：仅在连接 MySQL 数据源或复现实验数据时需要。CSV、Excel 和 SQLite 主路径不依赖 MySQL。

uv --version
node --version
pnpm --version

---

以下命令均在项目根目录执行。

### 1. 安装后端依赖（含开发/测试依赖）

```bash
uv sync --group dev
```

该命令会在项目根目录创建 `.venv/` 虚拟环境，并按 `pyproject.toml` 与 `uv.lock` 安装后端依赖（DuckDB、FastAPI、pandas、polars、scikit-learn、SQLAlchemy 等）以及 `dev` 组的开发测试依赖（mypy、pytest、ruff 等）。

### 2. 安装前端依赖

```bash
pnpm --dir frontend install --frozen-lockfile
```

严格按照 `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml` 锁文件安装 `frontend/` 下的依赖。

### 3. 安装浏览器测试运行时

```bash
pnpm --dir frontend exec playwright install chromium
```

安装浏览器端到端测试所需要的 Chromium（仅在执行端到端测试时需要，可跳过）。

```bash
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
```

`.env` 默认内容（见 `.env.example`）：

```ini
NORTHLIGHT_RUNTIME_ROOT=.runtime
NORTHLIGHT_MODEL_NAME=deepseek-v4-flash
NORTHLIGHT_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com
```

> 模型凭证不会写入源码包或 `.env`。需要在线对话时，启动后进入“设置 → 模型服务”，填写 API Key、模型名称和 Base URL，先执行连接测试再保存；凭证将作为权限为 `600` 的运行时文件保存在 `.runtime/` 中。这不影响本地确定性能力。

```bash

```

curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:5173/
```

### 停止

```bash

```

停止脚本不会删除 `.runtime/` 中的项目、数据源、模型、报告与设置。需要彻底重置时，先备份所需项目，再手动删除 `.runtime/`。

### 指定其他端口

若默认端口被占用，可指定另外一组端口启动：

```bash

### Olist 演示数据

```bash

pnpm --dir frontend build
NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost pnpm --dir frontend test:e2e
```

### 性能诊断（可选）

百万行数据性能诊断：

```bash

```

---

## 七、常见问题

- **API 未就绪**：查看 `.runtime/logs/api.log`，确认 8000 端口未被其他进程占用。
- **页面无法访问 API**：确认 5173 端口未被占用，并为 localhost 设置 `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`。
- **在线聊天提示没有凭证**：进入“设置”页完成模型连接测试；这不影响本地确定性能力。
- **报告没有图表**：报告只嵌入明确引用的图表产物。应先保存图表，再创建新报告版本。
- **数据源显示已变化**：重新执行画像后再查询，避免沿用过期字段基线。

header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

The DeepSeek Harness implementation checkout is at __FDE_APP_PATH__/. The checkout location and current working directory are separate values and may differ; never infer the working directory from this path. Use pwd to determine the current working directory. Use this checkout only to inspect or extend DSH itself.

You are interacting with the user through the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI at http://127.0.0.1:3080. When the user refers to "this page", "this GUI", or "this app" without naming another target, they mean this GUI. The browser provides no implicit DOM, route, or screenshot context. The client-plugin HMR receiver is active, but client-plugin changes reload without a refresh only while `pnpm run dev:web` is also running from this same checkout to rebuild their bundles; verify that watcher before promising automatic updates. Every other change — the apps/web shell and plain packages — requires rebuilding the affected Web artifacts and verifying this existing URL after a page refresh. Starting another server does not update this GUI. The apps/web Vite entry builds the shell but is not a standalone application because only dsh web injects window.__DSH_BOOT__. Do not start a replacement server unless the user asks; if one is needed, use a managed background job and verify its exact URL.

You are a coding agent powered by the deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp model. Your working directory is __FDE_WORKSPACE_PATH__.

Paths prefixed with @ are files explicitly referenced by the user. Use the read tool when their contents are needed; do not claim to have inspected a file before reading it.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use the web_search tool to discover current information on the web. The required queries array accepts 1–4 non-empty search queries; use a one-item array for a single search. It returns an optional answer plus a list of source URLs. Use the returned source snippets when available, and cite the relevant URLs as markdown links.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Use subagent_fork in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

When you successfully create or modify files, mention the primary outputs in your final response. To make those and any other changed-file references clickable in Web, format them as Markdown inline code using the exact file-tool path, or a basename when unique among the files changed in that turn.

tools.name: architecture_get
tools.description: Read the current FDE project system architecture and its exact revision before proposing changes.

tools.name: architecture_set
tools.description: Publish one complete candidate architecture for the current FDE project. Call architecture_get first and pass its exact expectedRevision.

expectedRevision.description: Exact revision from architecture_get; 0 when absent.

edges.description: Directed relationships between existing node ids.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

tools.name: eval_gate
tools.description: Compare an eval report against a baseline report and emit a CI gate verdict. OVERALL=PASS|WARN|FAIL|N/A; exit code semantics: PASS=0, FAIL=1, N/A=2, WARN=0 (2 in strict mode). Set gate_json=true for a single JSON object output. Omit before (or point it at a missing file) for N/A.

before.description: Path to the baseline report.json. Omit or point at a missing file for N/A.

strict.description: Strict mode: WARN exit code becomes 2 instead of 0.

gate_json.description: Output a single JSON object instead of key=value text lines.

max_token_increase_pct.description: Token total (input+output+reasoning) increase threshold in percent: an unchanged-status case exceeding it counts as a token regression (WARN). Default 50; 0 disables.

min_trial_success_rate.description: Reliability gate for trials cases (0-1, off by default): a case with a reliability block is WARNed when the one-sided 95% Wilson lower bound of its successRate falls below this value. Judges the lower bound, not the point estimate.

tools.name: eval_judge_validate
tools.description: Calibrate the LLM judge against a human-labeled set: run judgeOutput per label and report the confusion matrix with TPR (real failures caught) and TNR (real passes not wronged) separately — raw agreement is misleading when most labels pass. Labels file is JSONL, one {"rubric": string, "output": string, "expect": "pass"|"fail"} per line. Output is a JSON text report; calibrated=true only when both TPR and TNR meet their thresholds.

labels_path.description: Path to the human-labeled JSONL file.

tpr_threshold.description: Minimum TPR (real failures caught) for calibrated=true. Default 0.9.

tnr_threshold.description: Minimum TNR (real passes not wronged) for calibrated=true. Default 0.9.

tools.name: eval_run
tools.description: Run DSH plugin regression eval cases: load yaml cases from cases_dir, drive real headless dsh agent sessions (isolated session_root/workspace), collect session traces (session.jsonl or default session.jsonl.zstd, read directly), run assertions, and write report.json + report.md to output_dir. Timed-out cases still get their partial trace collected when available. Output is a JSON text summary.

output_dir.description: Directory where report.json and report.md are written.

session_root.description: Isolated session root for the eval runs (default: <output_dir>/.sessions).

profile.description: dsh profile used to run cases (default 'headless').

dsh_bin.description: dsh executable command, split on whitespace (default: env DSH_BIN or 'dsh' from PATH). Use 'npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh' when dsh is not installed globally.

concurrency.description: How many cases run in parallel (default 1, serial). Each case gets its own session root and workspace, so parallel runs are isolated.

retries.description: Global default retry-on-failure count (default 0, no retry). A case runs at most retries+1 attempts and stops at the first fully passing attempt; fail and error (incl. timeout) both trigger a retry. The per-case yaml retries field takes precedence over this value. Ignored for cases with trials > 1.

trials.description: Global default independent-trial count for reliability measurement (default 1, single run). With trials > 1, the case runs exactly trials isolated attempts (workspace reset before each, no retries) and the report gains a per-case reliability block (successRate / pass@k / pass^k); case status stays any-pass. The per-case yaml trials field takes precedence.

pass_k.description: k for pass@k / pass^k reliability metrics (default 2). Must not exceed the effective trials of any measured case.

tags.description: Comma-separated tag filter: only run cases whose yaml tags field contains at least one of these.

only.description: Comma-separated case names: only run these cases (exact match). Combined with tags as an intersection.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: openapi_call
tools.description: Call one operation declared and allowed by the current FDE project OpenAPI configuration.

api.description: Use project for the current FDE project.

tools.name: openapi_describe
tools.description: Describe one operation from the current FDE project, including parameters, request body, and responses.

api.description: Use project for the current FDE project.

tools.name: openapi_list
tools.description: List and search operations from the OpenAPI definition owned by the current FDE project.

api.description: Optional API id; the current project id is project.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

block.text:
The user wants me to improve the system architecture based on the confirmed requirements, solutions, and real source code. First I should call architecture_get to read the current version, then call architecture_set to submit a complete candidate. The revision they mention in the page is 1.

838: @router.get("/projects/{project_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}/data")
839: def artifact_data(
840:     project_id: str,
841:     artifact_id: str,
842:     repository: Annotated[Repository, Depends(repo)],
843:     limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=500)] = 200,
844:     offset: Annotated[int, Query(ge=0)] = 0,
845:     sort_by: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=240)] = None,
846:     sort_order: Annotated[str, Query(pattern="^(asc|desc)$")] = "asc",
847:     filter_column: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=240)] = None,
848:     filter_value: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=500)] = None,
849: ) -> dict[str, object]:
850:     try:
851:         artifact = repository.get_artifact(project_id, artifact_id)
852:         path = project_root(project_id) / artifact.path
853:         raw_columns = artifact.artifact_metadata.get("columns", [])
854:         columns = [str(column) for column in raw_columns] if isinstance(raw_columns, list) else []
855:         for requested in (sort_by, filter_column):
856:             if requested and requested not in columns:
857:                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown artifact column: {requested}")
858:         if path.suffix == ".parquet":
859:             connection = duckdb.connect()
860:             try:
861:                 where = ""
862:                 parameters: list[object] = [str(path)]
863:                 if filter_column and filter_value:
864:                     where = f" WHERE CAST({_quote_identifier(filter_column)} AS VARCHAR) ILIKE ?"
865:                     parameters.append(f"%{filter_value}%")
866:                 order = (
867:                     f" ORDER BY {_quote_identifier(sort_by)} {sort_order.upper()}"
868:                     if sort_by
869:                     else ""
870:                 )
871:                 total_row = connection.execute(
872:                     f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_parquet(?){where}", parameters
873:                 ).fetchone()
874:                 if total_row is None:
875:                     raise RuntimeError("Artifact count query returned no row")
876:                 total = int(total_row[0])
877:                 frame = connection.execute(
878:                     f"SELECT * FROM read_parquet(?){where}{order} LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
879:                     [*parameters, limit, offset],
880:                 ).df()
881:             finally:
882:                 connection.close()
883:         elif path.suffix == ".csv":
884:             full_frame = pd.read_csv(path)
885:             if filter_column and filter_value:
886:                 full_frame = full_frame[
887:                     full_frame[filter_column]
888:                     .astype("string")
889:                     .str.contains(filter_value, case=False, na=False, regex=False)
890:                 ]
891:             if sort_by:
892:                 full_frame = full_frame.sort_values(sort_by, ascending=sort_order == "asc")
893:             total = len(full_frame)
894:             frame = full_frame.iloc[offset : offset + limit]
895:         else:
896:             raise ValueError("Artifact does not expose tabular data")
897:         return {
898:             "artifact_id": artifact.id,
899:             "offset": offset,
900:             "limit": limit,
901:             "columns": list(frame.columns),
902:             "rows": frame_records(frame),
903:             "total": total,
904:         }
905:     except Exception as exc:
906:         raise handle_error(exc) from exc
907:

129: def classify_intent(message: str) -> Intent:
130:     normalized = message.lower()
131:     strong_data_anchor = any(
132:         term in normalized
133:         for term in ("当前数据", "这份数据", "数据集", "表中", "字段", "查询", "sql", "订单")
134:     )
135:     negative_operation = any(
136:         term in normalized
137:         for term in (
138:             "不要对当前数据",
139:             "不要查询",
140:             "不查询数据",
141:             "不需要查询",
142:             "不要访问数据",
143:             "不访问数据",
144:             "无需访问数据",
145:             "不要建模",
146:         )
147:     )
148:     explanatory_request = any(
149:         term in normalized for term in ("解释什么是", "写一段", "课程介绍", "概念介绍")
150:     )
151:     if negative_operation or (explanatory_request and not strong_data_anchor):
152:         return Intent.NORMAL
153:     for intent, terms in INTENT_TERMS.items():
154:         if any(term in normalized for term in terms):
155:             return intent
156:     return Intent.NORMAL
